overall: Atlanta had a classic summer convective day, with temperatures climbing steadily through the afternoon to a running maximum of 91.4°F observed around 16:00-17:00 ET — outperforming all three NWP models. A line of severe thunderstorms swept through around 17:00-18:00 ET (consistent with the active Severe Thunderstorm Warnings and Watch in effect), collapsing temperatures by more than 10°F in under an hour, with the 17:52 ASOS reading showing only 80.6°F. As of 19:10 ET, the temperature has partially rebounded to 82.4°F but the cooling trend (-1.8°F/hr velocity) and ongoing storm activity make any further peak highly unlikely.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance underforecast today's high across the board: ECMWF=87.5°F, NBM=86.8°F, and even the aggressive HRRR at 90.1°F fell short of the observed 91.4°F running maximum; only the HRRR came reasonably close. The give-up classifier fired at 14:40 ET when the running max was 89.6°F, but the temperature continued rising for roughly another 2-3 hours before the storm passage finally knocked it down — a reminder that convective days can sustain late afternoon surges even after early-fire signals.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high is almost certainly already locked in at 91.4°F. It is now past 19:00 ET, active thunderstorms are moving through the region, the temperature has fallen over 10°F from the peak, and the NWS Tonight forecast calls for continued storm chances and a low near 72°F — there is no credible pathway for temperatures to recover and exceed 91.4°F overnight. The INTRADAY model's 96.8% probability mass in the 90-91°F bucket (which covers this range) is consistent with this conclusion. Confidence is very high that 91.4°F is the final TMAX for today.
